knobs.note: BH-3545: at most this many NEW lead review requests a tick (a re-confirm of a head already requested does not count). The rest are deferred and seen again next tick, never dropped.
BH-3545: the per-PR tripwire. A PR that already had this many lead review requests in the last 24h gets no new one; one warn alert per PR per UTC day says so.

BH-5630: 1 restores the builder gate: a lead review is requested only for a head that carries a builder APPROVE (the in-build review, or review-prs). It protects a cheap first pass in front of the lead. Each firing costs a wait: every push from outside the pipeline leaves a head with no builder approval, and on 2026-10-08 that held 40-45 PRs for hours (skipped_no_approve=45). 0 (default) = one review gate: a head with no builder row, or with the builder APPROVE on an earlier head, is requested when CI is green on it (the lead lane's own lr_ci_green) and no lead, human or risk-tier verdict stands on it. A builder BLOCK is still skipped (the fix round owns it), and the risk tier never signs off such a head, except a lead-authored low rules-text head (BH-5325). Expected extra requests: the backlog of stuck heads once (about 45 on 2026-10-08), then about one per outside push; LEAD_REVIEW_ENQUEUE_MAX_PER_TICK and LEAD_REVIEW_MAX_PER_PR_DAY bound them.

BH-5779: how many times this lane resets a lead review request that came back failed for the current head, before it raises one alert (lead-failed-<slug>-<n>-<sha12>) that names the failure reason. 0 = never reset; the first failure alerts. A failed row with detail empty (billed, no verdict) is an environment failure: when bin/lead-review-land.sh registers LEAD_REVIEW_ENV_RETRY_MAX (BH-5793), that lane requeues it and this lane does not; on a tree without that knob, this lane resets it too, under this same cap.

BH-5795: 1 holds a lead review request for a head CI never tested: a DIRTY PR (GitHub runs no CI on it), or a PR whose base is not the default branch with no LEAD_REVIEW_TRACED_JOB check run that ran (none, all skipped, or unreadable). It protects the lead from reviewing a head no suite ran on: 22 review BLOCKs said exactly that (#4189..#5395). The hold dispatches LEAD_REVIEW_TRACED_WORKFLOW with scope=impact on the head branch once, and lasts at most LEAD_REVIEW_TRACED_MAX_WAIT_MIN; then the head is requested with the note `tests did not run`. Each firing costs that wait, at most. A PR on the default branch is never held: the merge-queue batch tests it. 0 = request as before.
BH-5795: the check-run name prefix of the CI job that runs the test suites (harness-ci.yml `Tests, traced (shard ...)`). LEAD_REVIEW_TRACED_WAIT reads it. Empty means this default.

BH-5795: the longest a head waits in the traced hold. After it the lead review is requested anyway and its scope note says `tests did not run: <reason>`, so no PR stalls on a run that never comes. It protects the review from running before the dispatched impact run (a few minutes). Each firing costs one review on a head with no test evidence, said in the note. 0 = off: no hold, the head is requested at once with the note.

BH-5795: the workflow file the traced hold dispatches with scope=impact on the held head's branch (one attempt per head). A repo without it answers 404; the hold then waits only for its bound. Empty means this default.

BH-5796: 1 holds a lead review request for a head that conflicts with its base: the conductor has it NEEDS_REBASE, REBASING or parked conflict-unresolvable, or GitHub lists it DIRTY, or `git merge-tree` on the hub clone's own objects (no fetch) names conflicted paths (main rewrote lines the PR also changes). It protects the lead from reviewing a head that must change before it can merge (8 review BLOCKs). Each firing costs a wait until the conductor or a fix round rebases it. 0 = request as before.

BH-5797: the silence check (bin/lib/silence-scan.sh, rules in catalog/silence-markers.tsv). 1 = a PR whose diff widens a public-leak allow-list (a KNOWN_FAKE_* entry in bin/share, a gitleaks marker) gets the needs-human label and one comment, and no lead review is asked until a person removes the label; every other allow-list line or lint marker goes into the lead review request notes for the Opus lead to judge (no human wait). It protects correctness and the public mirror: 5 of 295 BLOCK findings (2026-10 analysis) were a guard silenced to get green. A human-route firing costs a person's look and the PR's wait; a lead-route firing costs nothing extra. It reads no extra GitHub data (the compare the self check already fetched). 0 = off: every PR is requested as before, with no marker notes.

BH-5798: 1 runs the pre-review self-check (bin/pr-self-check.sh, rules in catalog/pr-self-check.tsv) on a PR body before a lead review is requested: Closes on a partial build, evidence on an older head, files outside the plan. It protects the lead from reviewing a body that does not match its head (38 review BLOCKs). Each firing costs a wait of at most PR_SELF_CHECK_MAX_WAIT_MIN, one fetch per held head per tick, and one PR comment per (head, body). 0 = request as before.

BH-5798: the longest a head waits on a refused self-check. After it the lead review is requested anyway, and its scope note carries `self-check: <findings>`, so no PR stalls on a body nobody fixes. 0 = off: no hold, the findings ride in the note at once.

BH-5581: protects the time from a head push to its lead re-review (median 16.8 min delta, 19.7 min full before this, n=57). Since BH-7235 nothing starts the pr mode: bin/wake-loop.sh no longer launches it, so this knob is read only by a hand run of bin/lead-review-enqueue.sh pr. Before that, on the hub, a pr synchronize/reopened/ready_for_review or check_suite.completed wake started bin/lead-review-enqueue.sh pr for that PR, and a head with a prior lead verdict on an earlier head is requested at once. Each firing costs one detached enqueue run on the hub: one open-PR list read per named repo, the PR body and verdict history reads, and at most one lead review request for a head the tick would request anyway. 0 = off: the */15 tick requests as before.
